items.title: Arthur "Monk" Hazel Interview, 1959-07-16
items.q: Harley is mentioned only as a bandleader ('Harley would play') in a story about Louis Armstrong and Bix Beiderbecke. The interviewee does not claim a personal relationship with Harley, only narrating that Harley's band played on the same boat.

ctx.x: He disputed that. He said the only old fae he ever played with was Bix. That's, that's, that's, that's not so. His mother had a card from Louie. And the card read, I, I read it with my, I saw it with my own eyes, Bill. The card read, now that the king is dead, I am the king. Signed, Louis Armstrong. That's what, it was a postcard. It wasn't a letter. Now from Bix, his mother had a whole letter of about a, about a full page letter saying how much he idolized Emmett, how much Emmett had done for him, both in…

temporary bandstand on the other side, where Harley would play, you see. And Harley only had seven men, and Fade had about ten or twelve men. So they got to playing, and the tune was high society. And Emmet was really blowing, and he was blowing so much so that they opened and instead of one, they had two spit valves on the horn. Two spit valves. He was blowing so hard he split both of them, his upper lip and his lower lip, too, from that all day, crying. And when he'd open up and let the water out of the horn,…
